solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Was head of detectives turned?

parts.note: to run something is to be in charge of it, so 'was head of' gives ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police's detective branch

explanation.surface: A question about whether a former chief of detectives has switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like a betrayal or change of direction; here it means gone sour, as milk turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone off, and butter or oil gone off is described as rancid.

clue.text: A major win, dispatching last couple in open court

indicators.note: dispatching means getting rid of, here the final two letters of the word

parts.note: a triumph is a great victory

explanation.surface: A big victory achieved, tossing aside the final pair in an outdoor tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIUMPH loses PH. 'open court' sounds like tennis but is an architectural space.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central courtyard or hall in a building, originally in a Roman house.

clue.text: Fellow space expert having half forgotten energy debacle

parts.note: cat is old slang for a man or fellow

indicators.note: half the word is forgotten, so only its first half is kept

parts.note: an astrophysicist studies the physics of stars and space
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A man who studies the cosmos forgets half his energy work, leading to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: ASTROPHYSICIST has 14 letters; keeping the first 7 gives ASTROPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure, so a catastrophe is a close synonym.

clue.text: Perhaps GP test includes name of creed

parts.note: a GP (general practitioner) is one kind of doctor, a doc

indicators.note: includes means contains, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A family doctor's exam features a religion's name.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside TRIAL to make TRINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrinal means relating to doctrine, a creed's body of beliefs.

clue.text: Put cloth cover on shivering dun horse

indicators.note: something shivering shakes about, so the letters of the two words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone throws a blanket over a cold, trembling greyish-brown horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges DUN HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shroud something is to wrap it in cloth, as a body is wrapped for burial.

clue.text: Obscure later note in financial district dishonesty

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, Britain's financial district

indicators.note: the note is said to be in the dishonesty, so it is placed within that word

parts.note: a lie is a piece of dishonesty
PS, postscript, is a note added later to a letter

explanation.surface: A memo hides fraud in the City's banking quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' is a verb here, to hide from view, not the adjective meaning little known. EC is the London postcode for the City.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to block it from view, so to obscure it.

clue.text: Serious honour senior accepts

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An elder solemnly takes a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober describes a serious, grave or restrained manner.

clue.text: Clear street crossing island

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so one piece straddles the other

parts.note: RD, short for road, stands in for a street

explanation.surface: A road is clear where it cuts across an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to clear it out, as in ridding a house of mice.

clue.text: Without improvement, varying sea level rises into crumbling dune

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other
crumbling sand breaks up, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: the tide is the rise and fall of the sea

explanation.surface: Coastal erosion: a changing tide washes into a collapsing sand dune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses the tide word because this is a down clue; 'crumbling' scrambles DUNE to UNED, and the reversed word goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Text that is unedited has not been revised or polished, so it is left without improvement.

clue.text: Expert not nerdy enough, ignoring repetitions of old rules?

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so these letters are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: someone not nerdy enough for a group is 'too cool'
O is the abbreviation for old; repeated, it gives two Os

explanation.surface: A specialist is judged insufficiently geeky, ignoring the repeated customs of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes two Os (O = old, repeated) from TOO COOL, leaving TOCOL. 'of old rules' reads as one phrase, but 'old' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the set of rules governing formal procedure or etiquette.

clue.text: Cheap Mac to acquire

parts.note: Mac and Bud are both casual ways of addressing a man, chiefly American
to get something is to acquire it

explanation.surface: A shopper wants to buy an inexpensive Apple computer or raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' looks like a computer or raincoat; it is a term of address for a man, like 'buddy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget is used as an adjective for low-priced goods, as in a budget airline.

clue.text: Cavalryman unwise to hold Soviet Union's leaders back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read from the end
to hold is to contain, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a rash decision is an unwise one

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A horse soldier is foolish enough to restrain the heads of the USSR.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' puts SU inside RASH, giving RASSUH, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a soldier of a light cavalry regiment, originally Hungarian.

clue.text: Trouble keeping half of common people in heating fuel

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pain is trouble or bother, as in 'a pain'

indicators.note: half of the word for common people, here its second half

parts.note: riffraff is a disparaging word for ordinary or disreputable people

explanation.surface: Something awkward involves the ordinary folk's share of oil for their stoves.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'half of' takes the second half of the synonym, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for kerosene, burnt in stoves and lamps.

clue.text: Vividly colourful bug on sources of metal coin

parts.note: a bug is a minor illness such as flu
ores are the rocks from which metals are extracted
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: An insect crawls over a bright metal coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sources of' looks like a first-letters signal, but ores are literally where metal comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorescent colours glow brightly, like highlighter pens and safety vests.

clue.text: Met objective the fuzz finally see, excited about that

indicators.note: about means going round, so the other pieces sit inside

parts.note: to rouse someone is to stir or excite them
an end is an aim or objective

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of each of the two words

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for 'see', used in references

explanation.surface: The police finally spot the goal and are agitated about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of both 'the' and 'fuzz'; 'that' is a link. 'Met' is not the Metropolitan Police but the past tense of meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendezvous as a verb means to meet at an agreed place, so having met is having rendezvoused.

clue.text: Unofficial law enforcer has criminal given tail

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An offender is given a tail, followed by a self-appointed lawman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges GIVEN TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes the law into their own hands without official authority.

clue.text: Agree to make up Spanish hero Quixote's ending

parts.note: to coin a word or phrase is to invent or make it up
El Cid was the medieval Castilian hero Rodrigo Díaz

indicators.note: ending means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Consenting to invent the end of Don Quixote's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that coincide match or correspond, so they agree.

clue.text: Doctor receiving sick people, collecting crowd's spit?

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the rest goes inside
collecting means gathering in, so the next piece is placed within the scramble
sick suggests something disordered, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: a gang is a crowd or group of people

explanation.surface: A GP sees unwell patients and gathers saliva from the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' scrambles the people word to OPPELE before the crowd goes inside. 'Spit' is short for 'the spitting image'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is a double or lookalike, which is what 'the spit' (spitting image) of someone means.

clue.text: Workshop more recently losing roof?

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: latelier is a jocular comparative of lately, meaning more recently

explanation.surface: A building that recently lost its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: LATELIER is a whimsical coinage; dropping its first letter L leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio or workshop.

clue.text: Female working, about to deliver hot dish

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
an expectant mother is due when about to give birth

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman still at work, close to giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver' looks like serving the food; it is childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondue is a dish of melted cheese or hot oil into which bread or meat is dipped.

clue.text: Persuade to use unfinished rail line's termini

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to rail is to complain bitterly, which is to inveigh

indicators.note: termini are end points, here the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Coaxing someone onto an incomplete railway's end stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like the railway, but it is the verb meaning to protest. 'unfinished' drops the H of INVEIGH; 'to use' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle someone is to coax or cajole them into doing something.

clue.text: Yard excavation turns frivolous

indicators.note: turns means the letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation

explanation.surface: Digging up the garden becomes a light-hearted pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Giddy describes someone flighty, silly or excitable, so frivolous.

clue.text: Sore loser's first returning racket

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken
returning means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A defeated tennis player throws a racket back, upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses NOISE to ESION. 'Sore' and 'racket' look like tennis; 'Sore' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or sore patch on the skin or an organ.

clue.text: Fantastic reptile with head becoming wide

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word is changed to another letter

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach

explanation.surface: An amazing lizard whose head grows broader.
explanation.walkthrough: W replaces the L of LIZARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Wizard is a dated British exclamation of approval meaning excellent or brilliant.

clue.text: Notices cause of cuts on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: an adze is a cutting tool, an axe-like blade for shaping wood

explanation.surface: Announcements on air explain why spending cuts are coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' suggests budget cuts; it means cuts made by a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ads, short for advertisements, are public notices.

clue.text: Something suggestive of ennui, waving with nod

indicators.note: waving moves things to and fro, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gesture hinting at boredom: a wave plus a nod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' rearranges ENNUI and NOD together.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, often sly or risqué, hint or insinuation.

clue.text: Answer in affirmative? Certainly right for me!

definitions.text: Answer in affirmative? Certainly right for me!

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: yes is the affirmative reply
aye is an old or Scots word for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone who always replies positively, exclaiming that everything suits them fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the sort of thing such a person would say; 'for me' completes that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A yea-sayer habitually agrees or says yes to everything, the sort who responds 'certainly, suits me'.

clue.text: Some like it here as one of a twosome

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people enjoy this place, as one half of a couple might.
explanation.definitionFit: Either refers to one or the other of two things, so it fits one member of a pair.
